title: Global Trends in Integrating Machine Learning (ML) with Model-Informed Drug Development (MIDD): A Bibliometric and Systematic Review (2015-2025)

content.abstract_summary: A combined bibliometric and systematic review of ML-MIDD research (2015–2025) using Web of Science, Scopus, and PubMed. Starting from 770 records, 607 unique publications were identified after deduplication; 560 met eligibility criteria. Findings: (1) ML-MIDD follows exponential growth (Price's Law) from 7 publications in 2016 to 159 in 2025 (22-fold); (2) US and China dominate output; (3) thematic evolution proceeds from foundational PK/PD-ML methods (2016–2018) → hybrid mechanistic-ML, deep learning, and RL (2022–2025); (4) formal regulatory endorsement of ML-MIDD as a standalone methodology has not yet occurred — ML components appear as adjuncts to established MIDD workflows in submissions. Tools: Bibliometrix, VOSviewer, PRISMA. PROSPERO registered: CRD420251276229.
key_findings: ML-MIDD publications follow exponential (Price's Law) growth: 7 articles in 2016 → 159 in 2025 (>22-fold increase); confirms the field is transitioning from early exploration to rapid maturation

Only 4.3% of publications were indexed in all three databases (Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed) — extreme fragmentation requires multi-database retrieval; using PubMed alone would miss >60% of relevant ML-MIDD literature

Top journals: CPT: Pharmacometrics & Systems Pharmacology (5.1%) and J Pharmacokinetics Pharmacodynamics (5.1%) — core pharmacometric venues anchor the field, but core journals account for only 28% of output

US leads (665 publications, 20.8%), followed by China (394, 12.3%) and France (180, 5.6%); US also leads citations (2,871) but citation leaders also include Switzerland and Germany despite lower volume

Most cited article in the corpus: Badillo et al. 2020 (Clinical Pharmacology & Therapeutics) with 303 citations — indicating that methodological reviews dominate citation impact, not primary empirical studies

Thematic evolution from 'machine learning' + 'PK/PD' + 'prediction' (motor themes 2019–2021) to 'machine learning' + 'humans' + 'personalized medicine' + 'pharmaco-omics' (2022–2025) — confirms shift from methods to clinical translation

No ML-MIDD approach has received standalone regulatory endorsement; FDA and EMA examples (Sotorasib, Abemaciclib, Lorlatinib) show ML as adjunctive tool within conventional MIDD, not as independent decision-making methodology

Hybrid mechanistic-ML models identified as the most impactful emerging paradigm: neural surrogate within PBPK workflows (Jia et al. 2025) achieved 2-fold accuracy across 106 test drugs; VAE for joint NLME parameter estimation and covariate selection in a single run
Global AI-in-pharma market: ~$1.94 billion in 2025 → ~$16.5 billion by 2034 (CAGR ~27%) — industry adoption context for the urgency of methodological standardization
Explainable AI (SHAP, LIME, counterfactuals) increasingly required to make ML-MIDD recommendations interpretable in pharmacological terms — a precondition for regulatory review
Drug development still costly and risky: mean cost ~$515.8 million per drug; ~90% of candidates fail in clinical development — the economic stakes motivating ML-MIDD investment
limitations: Database selection excludes preprints (bioRxiv, medRxiv), regulatory submissions, conference proceedings — may underrepresent industry-specific and very recent innovations
English-language restriction may omit non-English contributions; gray literature excluded
Bibliometric reliance on metadata accuracy; interdisciplinary ML-MIDD papers may be misclassified
No quantitative quality assessment of included studies — maps the landscape but cannot assess methodological rigor of individual works
Rapidly evolving field: search cutoff September 2025 means recent publications and regulatory developments not captured

extracted_claims.text: "The extent to which ML methods are explicitly integrated into regulatory decision-making remains limited and unevenly characterized."
"If only Web of Science had been used, 37% of relevant publications would have been lost. This loss would rise to more than 60% if PubMed were used as the sole source."
"The most impactful advances will likely come from coupling mechanistic models with ML surrogates or parsers, rather than treating ML as a purely black-box replacement."
"Regulatory acceptance of virtual bioequivalence relies heavily on the validation of computational models and the availability of accurate, comprehensive data inputs."

gaps_addressed: Quantifies the ML-MIDD landscape: 560 publications, 22-fold growth — establishes why MCS WG action is urgent and well-timed
Confirms that formal regulatory ML-MIDD integration has not occurred — the exact gap the WG's credibility framework operationalization work addresses
Hybrid mechanistic-ML (neural PBPK surrogates, VAE for NLME) identified as the most impactful paradigm — directly maps to WG Pillar 1
XAI (SHAP, LIME) required for regulatory review — confirms WG Pillar 2 focus on interpretability and UQ is not optional
RL for precision dosing is a documented thematic cluster in the corpus — confirms WG Pillar 3 is a recognized and growing research space
